2608.31097.title: Cross-Regional Grapevine Cold Hardiness Prediction via Learned Multimodal Latent Representations
2608.31097.paper_summary: Accurate daily predictions of cold hardiness in woody plants are critical in regions where freezing temperatures can damage dormant buds and reduce seasonal yield. Existing biophysical, hybrid, and deep learning models have shown high predictive accuracy when trained on local data but remain largely site-specific. The limited availability of cold hardiness data, coupled with the lack of principled methods for transferring cold hardiness predictions to new regions and cultivars, has limited the broader adoption and practical utility of these approaches, particularly in data-scarce regions. To address these limitations, we propose a cold hardiness prediction framework that learns a transferable latent representation by capturing region-specific variation through learned embeddings. To enable prediction in previously unseen regions, we infer embeddings from (1) text descriptions of the cultivar and growing region, and (2) limited historical observations, supporting both zero-shot and few-shot transfer. Experiments on datasets from six regions across North America demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art cold hardiness prediction methods, yielding more accurate predictions and substantially improving transfer to data-scarce regions.
2608.31097.paper_summary_zh: 準確的木本植物冷耐性的每日預測在凍結溫度可能損害休眠芽並減少季節性產量的地區至關重要。現有的生物物理、混合和深度學習模型在本地數據上訓練時顯示出高預測準確性，但仍然主要是特定於地點的。冷耐性數據的有限可用性，加上缺乏將冷耐性預測轉移到新地區和品種的原則性方法，限制了這些方法的更廣泛採用和實際效用，特別是在數據稀缺的地區。為了解決這些限制，我們提出了一個冷耐性預測框架，通過捕捉特定於地區的變異來學習可轉移的潛在表示，這是通過學習嵌入實現的。為了在以前未見的地區進行預測，我們從（1）品種和生長地區的文本描述，以及（2）有限的歷史觀察中推斷嵌入，支持零樣本和少樣本轉移。在北美六個地區的數據集上的實驗表明，我們的方法始終優於最先進的冷耐性預測方法，產生更準確的預測，並顯著改善向數據稀缺地區的轉移。
